headline: Anthropic had Claude produce roughly 180 million lines of proof code for open-source libraries
body: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team, working with partner Theorem, let Claude take over the proof work, The Decoder reports. The model produced roughly 180 million lines of mathematical proof code in just a few weeks, drawing on test programs from 123 open-source libraries. The proofs only hold under strict conditions, including a specific processor architecture and inputs under 64 MB.
note: The Decoder says formal verification was long reserved for extreme cases like Airbus avionics software, and Anthropic wants it to become as routine as standard testing.

evidence.text: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team , working with partner Theorem , let Claude take over the proof work instead.
The model produced roughly 180 million lines of mathematical proof code in just a few weeks, drawing on test programs from 123 open-source libraries in Google's OSS-Fuzz security project.
The proofs only hold under strict conditions: a specific processor architecture, single-threaded programs, and inputs under 64 MB.
Proving that software runs error-free under all circumstances has always been prohibitively expensive.
A team of specialists needed 20 person-years just to formally verify the small operating system kernel seL4, so the method was reserved for extreme cases like Airbus avionics software .
Anthropic wants formal verification with AI to become as routine as standard testing.
